title: Customer Relationship Management & Retention
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured Technical Sales Representative apprentice. Strategies for customer retention, upselling, and building long-term relationships with clients.
learning_objectives: Plan an account's first 90 days so the customer reaches value before the first renewal conversation
Use active listening in account reviews to surface risk the customer has not stated
Detect churn risk early and run a renewal conversation from evidence
Identify and qualify an upsell or cross-sell inside an existing account
Maintain account and opportunity records so the retention picture stays accurate
prerequisites: Introduction to Sales (se101), or equivalent sales fundamentals
Advanced SaaS Sales Strategies (se201), for retention and expansion metrics

sequencing_rationale: The course follows the account lifecycle in order: land and onboard (2), listen through the middle of the term (3), protect the renewal (4), then grow it (5), with the plan itself as the capstone (6). Expansion deliberately comes after renewal because selling more to an account that is quietly failing is the most common retention mistake this course exists to prevent. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS: the intake gives one sentence — retention, upselling, long-term relationships — for 16 hours. Scope was reconstructed from that plus the D4 competencies. Assumed in scope: the post-sale relationship a technical sales rep owns, including onboarding handoff, account reviews, renewal conversations, and expansion discovery. Assumed out of scope: customer-support operations and ticket handling, professional-services delivery, technical implementation work, and CRM mechanics (se301) — this course consumes the CRM rather than teaching it. Overlap with se201 lesson 6 is intentional and directional: se201 designs retention strategy from the economics, se310 executes it in conversation with the customer. Lesson 5 claims two course objectives because the upsell qualification and the record-keeping that supports it are assessed in the same exercise; the record-keeping objective is what D4-S1-C03 is tagged for in lessons 4 and 6.
